newsitem.title: SAO TOME AND PRINCIPE: China demands Sao Tome repays debt.
newsitem.headline: China demands Sao Tome repays debt.

text.p: China has urged the tiny West African island state of Sao Tome and Principe to repay a loan of $17 million after a break in diplomatic ties between the two countries, Sao Tomean officials said on Monday.
The officials said China had given the former Portuguese colony 90 days in which to repay the loan, which previously had a term of 30 years and an annual interest rate of three percent.
Sao Tomean Finance Minister Acacio Bonfim said he was "surprised" by the Chinese demand and lamented the decision.
Sao Tomean officials said they did not know what action China might take if the country failed to repay the loan, but they doubted the impoverished nation would be able to meet the new deadline.
Last month China suspended diplomatic relations with Sao Tome because it had set up official ties with Beijing's arch-rival Taiwan.

Taiwan sealed official links with Sao Tome and Principe in May when it set up an embassy there despite fierce protests from Beijing. China regards Taiwan as a rebel province not entitled to diplomatic ties. The two split in 1949 after a civil war.
